evidence.title: Threads and providers | Solenta docs

evidence.finding: Threads retain provider sessions, models and permissions; Claude and Codex support live steering, while other providers queue follow-ups.

evidence.finding: Local orchestrators fork worktree workers, communicate through MCP, collect results and integrate branches. Remote projects require plain threads by default.

evidence.title: Guardrails and verification | Solenta docs
evidence.finding: Verify command failure prevents green completion. Claude governance policies are limited to calls surfaced for approval.

evidence.title: Other computers and SSH | Solenta docs
evidence.finding: The app can install a Linux headless host over SSH; remote projects run CLIs there. Worktrees and orchestration remain local-only in v1.

evidence.title: Phones and browsers | Solenta docs
evidence.finding: Browser UI is served by the agent host with scoped device tokens, revocation and reconnect. Tailscale can provide HTTPS.

evidence.title: Worktrees and pull requests | Solenta docs
evidence.locator: Worktrees and pull requests; Development lanes
evidence.finding: Per-thread worktrees, staged diffs, inline review prompts, PR actions, checkpoints, JSON export and optional independent-provider review are documented.

evidence.title: External MCP pairing | Solenta docs
evidence.finding: External MCP clients can launch and inspect tasks with scoped expiring revocable tokens; new work defaults to approval.

evidence.title: Shared Memory for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor Agents
evidence.finding: Project-scoped local SQLite memory carries provenance and citations, invalidates stale file references, and injects recalled context into provider requests.

evidence.title: Inbox, Planboard, Review | Solenta docs
evidence.finding: The Planboard is GitHub/GitLab issues, not a local tracker. Auto-dispatch skips blocked issues; review queues group PR attention.

evidence.title: Spec mode | Solenta documentation
evidence.finding: Thread artifacts progress through approved requirements, design and tasks. Dependency-aware dispatch and Converge operate on the task DAG.

evidence.title: Skills | Solenta documentation
evidence.finding: Users can import skills, MCP configurations and instructions; plugin/local command trust is separate.

evidence.title: Automations | Solenta docs
evidence.finding: Schedules and polled GitHub, Linear and Sentry events start threads; three consecutive failures pause an automation.

evidence.title: Spend guardrails | Solenta docs
evidence.finding: Daily and orchestration budgets gate new work; a configurable concurrency cap queues runs oldest first.

evidence.title: Usage and fleet analytics | Solenta docs
evidence.finding: Usage separates provider/model costs and provider quota windows; estimated model prices fill missing costs and fleet metrics use Git/GitHub.

evidence.title: Review itinerary | Solenta docs
evidence.finding: Working-tree changes receive a risk-ranked review order that places CI/config changes first.

evidence.title: Architecture | Solenta docs
evidence.finding: Electron main manages processes, local storage and scheduling; the UI is React over typed IPC.

evidence.title: Solenta: run Claude Code, Codex and Cursor in parallel
evidence.finding: macOS Apple Silicon, Windows x64 portable and Linux glibc x64 downloads. The application is free and MIT licensed; agent subscriptions are separate.

evidence.title: Solenta changelog: release notes and new features
evidence.finding: Shipped provider accounts, local models, MCP controls, schedules and SSH teleport are listed in release notes.

evidence.title: Notifications and updates | Solenta docs
evidence.finding: Desktop completion/decision notifications and a morning digest summarize unattended work.

evidence.title: Build workflows | Solenta docs
evidence.finding: Sequential phases can fan out across providers, retry interrupted work and use versioned repository templates.

evidence.title: Codex sessions | Solenta docs
evidence.finding: Interactive Codex has live steering and approvals; noninteractive workflow phases lack live steering. Native session ownership is protected.

evidence.title: Import, eject and reclaim | Solenta docs
evidence.finding: Import provider history, eject to a terminal and reclaim outside turns without duplicate messages.

evidence.title: Project config files | Solenta docs
evidence.finding: Shared solenta.json and local overrides define setup, quick actions and automations with command trust checks.

evidence.title: Dev servers | Solenta docs
evidence.finding: Managed servers use per-thread environment paths, optional readiness probes, retained command output and cleanup.

evidence.title: Terminal and Browser panes | Solenta docs
evidence.finding: Per-thread shell and loopback browser provide previews, screenshots and agent-visible diagnostics.

evidence.title: Windows | Solenta documentation
evidence.finding: The Windows doctor checks Git Bash, Node 22, long paths and WSL boundaries.

evidence.title: Solenta README, usage ping
evidence.locator: README.md lines 338-341 (Usage ping) and electron/telemetry.js lines 9-23, release v0.29.0 commit f46d238
evidence.finding: Release builds send one anonymous usage ping a day (random install id, version, OS, architecture and agent CLIs used); setting DO_NOT_TRACK=1 or SOLENTA_TELEMETRY=0 turns it off, as the telemetry module checks.

evidence.title: Solenta download and offering list
evidence.locator: Download sections and FAQ: Does my code leave my machine; Do I pay Solenta for tokens; Is it free
evidence.finding: The official offering is a free MIT desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux, with browser access served by the user host. The complete download list has no iOS/Android app. The FAQ explicitly says there is no Solenta cloud and Solenta never resells tokens or sits in the billing path.

evidence.title: Solenta process confinement
evidence.locator: electron/sandbox.js locationReason, agentSandbox and resolveSandbox; runner.js and runner-seatbelt.js
evidence.finding: The scoped runner uses ordinary child processes locally, SSH hosts or WSL, with agent-specific permission flags and optional macOS Seatbelt wrapping. It has no product-provisioned container or per-agent VM execution backend. WSL host use is not a per-agent VM isolation option.

evidence.title: Solenta Planboard backing
evidence.locator: electron/issues.js createIssue and issue target routing; site/docs/views/index.html Planboard; store-normalize.js persisted data
evidence.finding: Planboard operations target GitHub/GitLab issues rather than product-owned issue records. Native state contains threads and spec artifacts, not a separate issue lifecycle. The docs explicitly describe the board as external issues.

evidence.title: Solenta shared device transport
evidence.locator: electron/webBridge.js authentication, invoke dispatch and wss.clients broadcasting; electron/webScopes.js; site/docs/web-mode/index.html Devices
evidence.finding: Multiple paired browser devices connect to the same host thread state. Steer/full-access tokens can send thread instructions and approve tool requests through the shared IPC handlers, while broadcasts reach authorized clients. Authentication is device-token based; there is no organization role or SAML/OIDC single-sign-on model in these modules.
